title: Evaluation Metrics — A Metric Is a Decision Contract
key_insight: Decision analysis assigns costs or benefits to outcomes and selects a threshold for that setting. Expected utility makes the tradeoff explicit.
body:
## A Metric Is a Decision Contract

Two hospitals value missed disease differently because follow-up cost and patient harm differ. No universal score can choose their operating point.

Decision analysis assigns costs or benefits to outcomes and selects a threshold for that setting. Expected utility makes the tradeoff explicit.

Confidence intervals and paired tests show whether a score difference is stable. Segment results reveal whether an average gain hides harm to a subgroup.
common_mistakes: Using accuracy for a rare positive class.
Comparing AUC without choosing a deployment threshold.
Treating a tiny metric difference as meaningful without uncertainty.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “A Metric Is a Decision Contract” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: The wrong metric rewards the wrong model, especially with rare events.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “A Metric Is a Decision Contract” story, explain Evaluation Metrics without assuming the listener knows machine learning.
